hiddenNotes: Published tuition ranges widely: about 25,000 dollars at public universities (the out-of-state rate international students pay) to 45,000-plus at private ones, so the figure here is a representative midpoint.
US universities require their own health insurance and often auto-enroll you in a plan costing 1,500 to 2,500 dollars a year, on top of any cover you arrange yourself.
There is little need-based aid for international undergraduates, and all-in costs at top private universities can exceed 80,000 dollars a year.

The proof-of-funds requirement more than doubled to CAD 22,895 per year for a single student outside Quebec, far above the roughly CAD 10,000 many families still budget for.
Ontario's UHIP health insurance is mandatory and rises to about CAD 948 for 2026/27, and it excludes dental, prescription drugs, and mental health unless you add supplementary cover.
Tuition here is the national average for international undergraduates; high-demand programs and top universities charge considerably more.
